NEW YORK/JOHANNESBURG, NOVEMBER 26 — In advance of World AIDS Day on December 1, Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is once again calling for more people globally to have access to the highly effective HIV prevention medicine lenacapavir . This twice-yearly injectable version of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is the biggest breakthrough in HIV prevention yet, but US-based Gilead Sciences continues to block affordable access for countries around the world. events.title: Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF): 2026 First Reserve Allocation Strategy (US Special Reserve Tranche I)
events.summary: Country: Syrian Arab Republic Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs Please refer to the attached file. In a context emerging from years of largescale conflict, where some conditions have improved but localized violence, new and secondary displacement, and very high humanitarian needs persist in parts of the country, this allocation will fast-track lifesaving and life sustaining multisectoral assistance and protection for crisis affected people in 85 priority subdistricts, which record the highest intersectoral severity of needs and the highest prevalence of IDPs and returnees. The allocation will support the immediate kickstart of the hyper prioritized HNRP, targeting around 4.3 million women, men, girls, boys, older people and persons with disabilities with direct assistance in areas with the highest concentrations of IDPs, returnees and refugees. In this way, the Syria Humanitarian Fund will help translate the humanitarian reset roadmap into concrete action, using pooled funding to drive a principled, highly prioritized and locally empowered response: channeling resources to the most severe needs at speed and scale, minimizing layers and passthrough funding, enabling integrated and multisector programming by best placed actors, and strengthening collective accountability through transparent, evidence based allocation, enhanced monitoring and improved accountability to affected populations. Taken together, the fast‑track reserve, the CERF UFE allocation and the first SHF Standard Allocation form a single, sequenced funding package of over US$200 million designed to save lives in the first half of 2026, while structurally advancing localization through a target of around 75 per cent of SA1 resources to national NGOs and women‑led organizations.

INTRODUCTION In response to the Ministry of Interior's (MoI) decision of 26 September 2023 to enact an “Illegal Foreigners' Repatriation Plan”, UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency and IOM, the UN Migration Agency, have collated their data on the arrest, detention, and deportation of Proof of Registration (PoR) holders, Afghan Citizen Card (ACC) holders, and undocumented Afghan nationals as well as on the outflows of Afghan nationals at the Torkham, Ghulam Khan, Chaman, Badini and Bahramcha border crossing points, to better understand the protection environment and movements of Afghan nationals returning to Afghanistan from Pakistan. n 2025, the Government of Pakistan (GoP) issued several directives impacting Afghan nationals. In January, the GoP announced that Afghan nationals should relocate from Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) and Rawalpindi, or else face deportation. In April, further announcements indicated the implementation of the second phase of the “IFRP”, targeting ACC holders, in addition to undocumented Afghans. In July, the GoP issued a Statutory Regulation Order (SRO) directing the repatriation/deportation of PoR card holders following the expiry of PoR card validity on 30 June. The GoP later indicated a deadline of 1 September for PoR holders to leave Pakistan, before the start of the repatriation/deportation process. UNHCR issued a press briefing expressing concern regarding the decision and urging the GoP to exempt Afghans with international protection needs, as well as those with particular circumstances or vulnerabilities, from involuntary return.

events.title: DR Congo: Cluster Protection RDC : Points saillants de la situation de protection en République démocratique du Congo du mois d'octobre 2026
events.summary: Country: Democratic Republic of the Congo Source: Protection Cluster Please refer to the attached Infographic. Au cours du mois d’octobre 2026, la situation de protection en République démocratique du Congo est restée fragile et volatile, particulièrement dans l’Est du pays, où la poursuite des affrontements armés, l’activisme des groupes armés et les tensions sécuritaires ont continué d’exposer les populations civiles à de graves violations des droits humains. Malgré la poursuite des initiatives diplomatiques et des efforts de médiation régionaux et internationaux, les dynamiques de conflit observées sur le terrain n’ont montré que peu de signes d’apaisement, notamment dans les provinces de l’Ituri, du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu. L’environnement de protection a été marqué par des homicides, des enlèvements, des violences sexuelles, des violations graves des droits de l’enfant, des pillages, des destructions de biens ainsi que des restrictions de mouvement affectant l’accès des populations aux services essentiels et aux moyens de subsistance. Les personnes déplacées internes, les retournés, les femmes et les enfants demeurent parmi les catégories les plus exposées. Around 862,791 refugees from Ukraine are currently present in Poland, the majority women and children. This represents some 2.5 per cent of the total population of Poland. UNHCR coordinates the response of 58 organizations in Poland under the Ukraine Situation Regional Refugee Response Plan (RRP), the majority of which are local and refugee-led organizations. UNHCR works with the Government of Poland to ensure refugees have access to territory, legal status, documentation and enjoy their rights. HIGHLIGHTS Strengthening access to legal information amid changes to Temporary Protection (TP) Following the entry into force of the Phasing Out Act on 5 March 2026, significant changes were introduced to the temporary protection legal framework in Poland, impacting access to collective accommodation and social assistance with the new eligibility requirements for healthcare coverage. In response, UNHCR scaled up legal information and assistance to help refugees navigate the new framework. Through its eight legal partner organizations, UNHCR provided timely information on changes to temporary protection, including new identity verification requirements for temporary protection holders across Poland.
